Same tax zone as Vancouver Unlike the price, the tax in a Surrey litre is known exactly. The TransLink service area covers the municipalities of Metro Vancouver, Surrey among them, and gasoline sold there carries 27 cents of motor fuel tax per litre, with 18.5 cents going to TransLink. Drive east past the regional boundary and the rate drops to the provincial 14.5 cents; in the Victoria area it is 20 cents. GST at 5% applies on top of the price with those taxes, and B.C. charges no provincial sales tax on road fuel. Since the carbon tax ended on April 1, 2025 and the federal excise was suspended on April 20, 2026, the fixed tax in a Surrey litre is the TransLink-area motor fuel tax alone. The Kelowna page shows what the same litre pays outside the two transit zones. A year of driving in Surrey For a commuter, the yearly bill depends far more on the vehicle than on small differences between stations. Over 20,000 km a year at the estimate for October 22, 2026, a compact car rated 8.7 L/100 km needs about $3,689 of fuel, a full-size pickup rated 12.9 L/100 km about $5,470. Pick your own class and distance below. Those consumption figures are the median combined ratings of 2026 models in each class, published by Natural Resources Canada. Real consumption in heavy commuting traffic is usually above the label, so treat the result as a floor. The past year and your next fill-up The Vancouver series is published under the Open Government Licence, so the last months can be shown here. They are the same numbers as on the Vancouver page , since Surrey shares the average. If the station sign shows a different price from the estimate, use it: the calculator below gives the cost of your tank and what each cent per litre is worth. Is there an official gas price for Surrey? Not a separate one. Statistics Canada publishes a monthly average for the Vancouver area, which includes Surrey, and that is the figure used here. Weekly averages from Natural Resources Canada also exist but cannot be republished. Individual stations in Surrey can sit a few cents above or below that regional average, so read it as a benchmark against the posted price. Do Surrey drivers pay the TransLink gas tax? Yes. Surrey is one of the municipalities of the TransLink service area, so gasoline sold there carries the full Metro Vancouver rate of 27 cents per litre of motor fuel tax, 18.5 of which fund TransLink. Leaving the region changes that: the Fraser Valley outside Metro Vancouver pays the provincial rate of 14.5 cents. How much does a year of fuel cost a Surrey commuter? It depends mostly on the vehicle. The budget calculator on this page uses the median combined rating of 2026 models in each class, from Natural Resources Canada, and prices the litres at the estimate for tomorrow. At the median ratings, a full-size pickup burns 1.5 times as much fuel as a compact car over the same distance, so the vehicle matters more than the station.

victoria/en.text: Regular gasoline averaged 210.0¢/L in Victoria in September 2026; brought to October 22, 2026, the estimate is 212.5¢/L. Victoria has its own Statistics Canada series, published monthly, and its latest month is September 2026: 210.0¢/L a litre for regular gasoline and 278.3¢/L for diesel, taxes included. That is 0.5¢/L above Vancouver the same month, even though a Victoria litre pays 20 cents of motor fuel tax against 27 on the mainland: before tax, the island's fuel costs more. The page moves the monthly average to October 22, 2026 with the Edmonton wholesale price and dated tax changes, which gives 212.5¢/L; over 25 months of history, this estimate was off by 6.8¢/L on average, compared with 8.8¢/L for a simple repeat of the last month. Of the 20 cents, 5.5 fund BC Transit in the Victoria region; GST at 5% comes on top, and taxes make up 14.2% of the estimate. Victoria's own monthly series Victoria is a separate line in the Statistics Canada table of retail fuel prices. It is a monthly average, so the newest figure always trails by several weeks; on October 21, 2026 it is the September 2026 average. The table gives each fuel with that month and the estimate for October 22, 2026. The estimate starts from the month and adds the change in the Edmonton rack price published since, plus GST, and any tax change dated in between. No B.C. tax changed between that month and tomorrow, so for Victoria the estimate moves with the wholesale market only. Island price, lower tax The two B.C. cities with a transit fuel tax make a useful comparison, because their tax is known to the tenth of a cent. At the September 2026 averages, tax takes 30.0¢/L of a Victoria litre and 37.0¢/L of a Vancouver litre. What remains, the product and margins, is 7.5¢/L higher in Victoria. That pre-tax gap is what drivers on the island pay for their market, and it explains why a lower tax does not always mean a lower pump price. The comparison uses the estimates for both cities, built from the same Edmonton rack price, so the gap it shows is the one between the two monthly averages carried forward. For cities in the Okanagan and the north, which pay neither transit levy, see the Kelowna page . Where the 20 cents go Gasoline sold in the Victoria regional transit area pays 20 cents of motor fuel tax per litre: the provincial rate of 14.5 cents charged throughout B.C., and 5.5 cents for BC Transit. Diesel pays 20.5 cents. GST at 5% is charged on the price including those cents, and B.C. charges no provincial sales tax on fuel. The B.C. carbon tax, which used to be a separate line, was eliminated on April 1, 2025. The federal excise tax has been suspended since April 20, 2026, and its return is the next dated change that will move the Victoria price. The excise return in 2027 Finance Canada's draft legislation extends the suspension to January 31, 2027, then charges half the excise in February and March 2027 and all of it from April 1, 2027: 10 cents a litre on gasoline and 4 on diesel, before GST. For a household that buys a given number of litres each month, the calculator shows the extra cost. The draft schedule is not yet law; the forecast page follows it, and the tax page lists every rate by province. Thirteen months in Victoria The Statistics Canada series is under the Open Government Licence, so its recent months are shown below, newest first. Why is gas so expensive in Victoria when its tax is lower than Vancouver? Victoria's motor fuel tax is 20 cents a litre, 7 cents below Metro Vancouver, yet its average pump price can be close to Vancouver's. When it is, the difference sits in the product share: once taxes are removed, a litre on southern Vancouver Island costs more than one on the mainland. No official source breaks that pre-tax cost down by city, so the page shows the gap without guessing its causes. What is the BC Transit gas tax in Victoria? In the Victoria regional transit area, 5.5 cents of every litre of gasoline go to BC Transit. Added to the 14.5-cent provincial motor fuel tax, that makes 20 cents per litre, before GST. The rate is the same for every station in the area, so it does not explain price differences between stations, only the gap with the rest of the province. How much will the federal excise add to gas in Victoria in 2027? Under Finance Canada's draft legislation, the 10-cent federal excise tax on gasoline, suspended since April 20, 2026, returns at half rate on February 1, 2027 and in full on April 1, 2027. With 5% GST on top, the full rate adds 10.50¢/L per litre in B.C. The calculator on this page turns that into dollars a month for your own consumption.

kelowna/en.text: Kelowna has no freely reusable official gas price, but each litre carries a known 14.5 cents of B.C. fuel tax plus 5% GST, less than in Vancouver or Victoria. No public agency publishes a Kelowna gas price under a licence that allows it to be reproduced. Statistics Canada's monthly averages cover Vancouver and Victoria in British Columbia, not the Okanagan, and Natural Resources Canada's weekly city averages, which do list Kelowna, may be consulted but not republished, so this page links to them instead of copying them. What can be stated precisely is the tax. Outside Metro Vancouver and the Victoria area, a litre of gasoline in B.C. carries the provincial motor fuel tax of 14.5 cents, with no transit levy, and 5% GST is charged on the full price; the federal excise tax is at zero since April 20, 2026 and the B.C. carbon tax ended on April 1, 2025. That puts Kelowna 12.5 cents a litre below Metro Vancouver's 27 cents and 5.5 cents below the Victoria area's 20 cents before GST, or 13.13¢/L and 5.78¢/L with it. For a price, use the calculator with the figure on the sign: it opens at the Vancouver estimate of 212.0¢/L only as a starting point. Why this page has no Kelowna average A price page is only as good as its source. For Kelowna, the open sources run out. Statistics Canada's table 18-10-0001-01, the monthly series this site uses for western cities, includes Vancouver and Victoria for British Columbia but not the Okanagan. Natural Resources Canada does collect weekly averages by city, Kelowna among them, but those figures are not published under a licence that lets this site republish them. You can read them directly at the source: Natural Resources Canada, average retail prices by city . The page therefore does three things it can do with certainty: it states the tax that applies in Kelowna, it compares that tax with the two B.C. areas that pay more, and it turns the price on a sign into the cost of a fill-up. The tax in a Kelowna litre Kelowna is outside both B.C. transit tax areas, so only the provincial motor fuel tax applies per litre. GST then applies on the full price, including that tax. Provincial sales tax does not apply to road fuel in British Columbia. To find the GST inside a posted price, divide it by 21: at 212.0¢/L, it is 10.10¢/L. The share of tax in the price then follows from what you pay; at that same price, it would be 11.6%. Kelowna against Vancouver and Victoria The two other B.C. regions add their own transit tax to the provincial rate. The comparison below is for tax only, not for the pump price. For reference, the site's estimates for October 22, 2026 are 212.0¢/L in Vancouver and 212.5¢/L in Victoria , both brought forward from a Statistics Canada monthly average. Subtracting the tax gap from them does not give a Kelowna price: transport from the supply terminals, competition among stations and retail margins differ in the Okanagan, and no open data measures them. Your fill-up in Kelowna The calculator at the top of the page and the one below start from the Vancouver estimate only so that they show a realistic result; replace it with the price on the sign. A 65-litre SUV tank at 212.0¢/L costs $137.80, and every cent per litre changes that by $0.65. The excise in 2027 The federal excise tax, 10 cents a litre on gasoline before April 20, 2026, is planned to return at half rate on February 1, 2027 and in full on April 1, 2027. With GST, the full return adds 10.50¢/L in Kelowna. For western cities that do have a published average, see Calgary , where Alberta's fuel tax relief changes the picture, and the provincial tax comparison . Why is there no official average gas price for Kelowna on this page? Statistics Canada publishes monthly averages for Vancouver and Victoria only in British Columbia. Natural Resources Canada does publish weekly averages that include Kelowna, but their terms do not allow them to be reproduced, so the page links to them. Rather than invent a figure, it gives the exact taxes and a calculator for the price you see posted. How much tax is in a litre of gas in Kelowna? B.C.'s motor fuel tax is 14.5 cents a litre on gasoline and 15.0 cents on diesel in Kelowna, with no regional transit tax. GST at 5% is added on the full price, which at a posted 212.0¢/L is 10.10¢/L. The federal excise is suspended until at least January 31, 2027. Should gas in Kelowna be cheaper than in Vancouver? On tax alone, yes: Metro Vancouver adds a 12.5-cent TransLink tax that Kelowna does not pay, worth 13.13¢/L with GST. The pump price also depends on transport from the supply terminal, local competition and retail margins, which this site cannot measure for Kelowna, so the real gap can be smaller or larger. How much will the 2027 excise return add in Kelowna? Under Finance Canada's draft legislation the federal excise on gasoline comes back at 5 cents on February 1, 2027 and 10 cents on April 1, 2027. With 5% GST on top, that is 5.25¢/L and then 10.50¢/L in Kelowna, the same as anywhere in B.C.

calgary/en.text: With the Alberta fuel tax not collected, regular gasoline in Calgary is estimated at 156.1¢/L for October 22, 2026, against a September 2026 average of 167.3¢/L. Calgary's open official gas price is the Statistics Canada monthly average, and the latest month published is September 2026: 167.3¢/L a litre for regular, 193.6¢/L for premium and 240.8¢/L for diesel. Since then, one thing has changed by law: under Alberta's Fuel Tax Relief Program, the 13-cent provincial fuel tax is not collected from October 1, 2026 to at least December 31, 2026. With GST, that removes 13.6¢/L from a litre. The page also moves the monthly figure with the Edmonton wholesale price, and the result for October 22, 2026 is 156.1¢/L for regular. Over 25 past months, the method missed the next Statistics Canada figure by 1.9¢/L on average, against 6.5¢/L for repeating the last month. With the Alberta tax and the federal excise both at zero for now, the only tax left in a Calgary litre is the 5% GST, 4.8% of the estimated price. A tax holiday the monthly average cannot see Statistics Canada publishes Calgary's average pump price once a month, weeks after the month ends. Its latest figure, for September 2026, still includes the Alberta fuel tax of 13 cents a litre. That tax stopped on October 1, 2026 under the province's Fuel Tax Relief Program, so any reading of the September 2026 number as "today's price" would overstate it. The estimate column corrects for that. For regular, the correction for the tax is −13.6¢ at the pump, GST included. The Edmonton rack price, published every business day by the Government of Ontario, then adds +2.5¢ for the wholesale movement since September 2026. The calculator below lists those parts with their dates. The Fuel Tax Relief Program Alberta ties its fuel tax to the price of oil. While the relief program applies, the 13-cent rate is not collected, and the province has said that will last until at least December 31, 2026. From January 1, 2027 at the earliest, the rate will be set at 0, 4.5, 9 or 13 cents depending on the price of WTI crude, and it cannot climb by more than 9 cents from one quarter to the next. That leaves a Calgary litre with the 5% GST as its only tax for the moment: 7.4¢/L at the estimated price. No transit levy applies in Alberta and there is no provincial sales tax. This page will show the new Alberta rate as soon as it is published, and the forecast page follows both dated changes coming in 2027. Two taxes that could come back in 2027 The federal excise tax of 10 cents a litre on gasoline has been suspended since April 20, 2026. Finance Canada's draft legislation brings it back at half rate on February 1, 2027 and in full on April 1, 2027. In Alberta, that return could coincide with a quarterly reset of the provincial tax, so a Calgary driver may see two increases in the first half of 2027. The calculator below measures the federal part alone for your monthly consumption. If Alberta restores its full 13 cents at some point, the combined effect with the full excise would be 24.15¢/L per litre with GST, all else equal. Whether and when that happens depends on the oil price and the province's quarterly decisions. Calgary over the last thirteen months The Statistics Canada series is published under the Open Government Licence and appears in full below. Over the period, the highest monthly average was 176.9¢/L in May 2026 and the lowest 114.9¢/L in December 2025. For the latest tomorrow figures of every city, see the tomorrow page ; for a side-by-side with the capital, the Edmonton page . Is the Alberta fuel tax still suspended in Calgary? Yes, for now. Under the Fuel Tax Relief Program, the 13-cent tax is not collected from October 1 to at least December 31, 2026. From January 1, 2027 at the earliest, the rate will depend on the price of WTI oil: 0, 4.5, 9 or 13 cents, and it can rise by no more than 9 cents in one quarter. The page dates each step as the province confirms it. Why is the Calgary estimate lower than the last Statistics Canada average? Because the last average is for a month when the Alberta fuel tax was still collected. The estimate removes that tax, with the GST charged on it, from the day it stopped. It also adds the change in the Edmonton wholesale price since that month, which can push the figure up or down. The tomorrow calculator on this page shows each part separately. Are Calgary gas prices higher than Edmonton? In 13 of the 13 monthly Statistics Canada averages shown on this page, Calgary was above Edmonton. Both cities pay exactly the same taxes, so any gap is in the product and the retail margins. The Edmonton page compares the two cities with today's estimates and explains why Edmonton's wholesale price is the reference for every western estimate on this site.

edmonton/en.text: Edmonton regular gasoline is estimated at 151.3¢/L for October 22, 2026, the cheapest of the 7 western cities with their own official series. Edmonton plays two roles on this site. Like every western city, its official open price is the Statistics Canada monthly average, 162.5¢/L a litre for regular and 236.0¢/L for diesel in September 2026. It is also the wholesale reference: the Government of Ontario publishes a daily rack price for Edmonton, and that price is what carries every western monthly average forward to today. For Edmonton itself, the rack change since September 2026 and any dated tax change, such as the suspension of the 13-cent Alberta fuel tax on October 1, 2026, give an estimate of 151.3¢/L for October 22, 2026. Tested on 25 months, this method was off by 2.4¢/L on average, where repeating the previous month was off by 6.4¢/L. That puts Edmonton the cheapest among the 7 western cities with a series of their own. While the Alberta tax and the federal excise are not collected, GST is the only tax in the litre: 4.8% of the estimate. The wholesale hub behind every western estimate A monthly average is a good benchmark and a poor price for today. To bring it forward, the site needs a daily market signal for Western Canada, and the only open one is the Edmonton rack price published by the Government of Ontario. Its value on October 14, 2026 was +2.4¢ away from its September 2026 average, which becomes +2.5¢ at an Alberta pump once GST is added. The same movement feeds the estimates for Vancouver, Calgary, Regina, Saskatoon and Winnipeg. The rack price is published about a week late, so the estimate knows the market up to that day and not beyond. Its measured error, shown in the last column, is the honest test of that limitation: it compares each past estimate with the Statistics Canada average that followed. Where Edmonton ranks in the West Among the 7 western cities that have a Statistics Canada series of their own, Edmonton is the cheapest at the estimates for October 22, 2026, with Edmonton lowest at 151.3¢/L and Victoria highest at 212.5¢/L. Tax is a large part of that spread: Alberta currently charges only GST, while B.C. cities carry transit fuel taxes and Saskatchewan and Manitoba charge their own provincial rates. The full Canada ranking adds Ontario, Quebec and the Atlantic provinces. Edmonton and Calgary Both Alberta cities pay identical taxes, and their estimates rely on the same rack price, so the comparison isolates the retail market. At the estimates for October 22, 2026, Calgary is 4.8¢/L higher. The Calgary page looks in detail at the Alberta fuel tax relief, which stopped the 13-cent provincial tax on October 1, 2026, and at what the oil-price formula could mean from January 2027. Tax in an Edmonton litre For now, an Edmonton litre of gasoline carries no per-litre tax at all: the Alberta fuel tax is not collected under the relief program and the federal excise has been suspended since April 20, 2026. The 5% GST, 7.2¢/L at the estimated price, is the only line left. Diesel in Edmonton At the estimates for October 22, 2026, diesel costs 79.1¢/L more than regular in Edmonton. With the same per-litre taxes on both fuels in Alberta at the moment, that gap is entirely the product. The monthly diesel series below shows how it has moved; from September 2025 to September 2026, the Edmonton diesel average changed by +100.9¢. The diesel page compares that spread across Canada, and the Saskatoon page covers the nearest market to the east. Why does this site use the Edmonton rack price for western cities? Edmonton is the refining and pipeline hub of the Prairies, and the Government of Ontario publishes a daily wholesale (rack) price for it under an open licence. This site has found no other open daily price for Western Canada. The estimate for Vancouver, Calgary, Regina or Winnipeg adds the change in that Edmonton price since the last monthly average, so it captures market moves without inventing a local figure. Is gas cheaper in Edmonton than in Calgary? The two cities pay exactly the same taxes, so the difference is in the product and retail margins. The comparison on this page uses the estimates for both cities, built from the same monthly source and the same rack price, so the gap it shows is like for like. Station prices within each city vary by more than that average gap. How much more does diesel cost than gasoline in Edmonton? Diesel follows its own refinery market, and in Alberta it pays the same taxes as gasoline per litre while the provincial fuel tax and the federal excise are at zero. So the whole gap between the two fuels in Edmonton comes from the product. The page shows that gap at today's estimates and the monthly diesel averages of Statistics Canada for the past year.

regina/en.text: From a September 2026 average of 174.0¢/L, regular gasoline in Regina is estimated at 176.5¢/L for October 22, 2026. Statistics Canada publishes one open official gas price for Regina, a monthly average, and its most recent month is September 2026, at 174.0¢/L a litre for regular and 241.0¢/L for diesel. To give a figure for today, the page adds the change in the Edmonton wholesale (rack) price since that month, with 5% GST: the estimate for October 22, 2026 is 176.5¢/L. On 25 months of history, that estimate was off by 3.6¢/L on average, against 6.1¢/L for assuming no change. Saskatchewan levies a fuel tax of 15 cents a litre on gasoline and diesel and does not charge its provincial sales tax on road fuel, so a Regina litre carries that tax and GST: 13.3% of the estimated price. The federal excise tax is suspended since April 20, 2026; when the draft schedule restores it in full on April 1, 2027, it will add 10.5¢/L a litre with GST. The Regina figure and how old it is Regina's official benchmark is monthly. Statistics Canada publishes it a few weeks after each month closes, so on October 21, 2026 the newest month is September 2026. The estimate column moves that figure with the Edmonton rack price, which the Government of Ontario publishes daily with about a week of delay, and with any tax change dated after the month. Weekly city prices from Natural Resources Canada exist, but their terms do not allow them to be copied here; the NRCan weekly table can be read on its own site. Saskatchewan's fuel tax Saskatchewan's fuel tax is 15 cents a litre for gasoline and diesel alike, and it is the same in Regina as anywhere else in the province: there is no transit or municipal surcharge. The provincial sales tax is not charged on road fuel. GST at 5% is, on the price that already includes the 15 cents, which is 8.4¢/L at the estimated price. The tax page sets that rate against the other provinces. Compared with Alberta, where the provincial fuel tax is not collected at the moment, a Regina litre carries 15.8¢/L more tax including GST. A year behind the wheel of a pickup For a driver who covers long distances in a truck, the yearly bill is what counts. A full-size pickup with the median 2026 rating of 12.9 L/100 km, driven 25,000 km a year, burns about 3,225 litres. At the Regina estimate for October 22, 2026, that is $5,692 a year, and each 10 cents per litre moves it by $323. The ratings come from Natural Resources Canada's fuel consumption guide for 2026 models. Towing, winter driving and gravel roads push real consumption above them. When the excise returns Finance Canada's draft legislation keeps the federal excise at zero until January 31, 2027, then charges half of it in February and March and all 10 cents from April 1, 2027. For the pickup above, the full rate with GST would add $339 over a year. The calculator measures it for your own monthly litres. The draft is not law yet; the forecast page follows it. Regina, Winnipeg and the past year At the estimates for October 22, 2026, Regina is 2.5¢/L above Winnipeg , the next capital to the east, and Saskatoon has its own page. The Statistics Canada series for Regina is published under the Open Government Licence: How much is the gas tax in Regina? Saskatchewan charges a fuel tax of 15 cents per litre on gasoline and on diesel, the same across the province, with no city or transit levy in Regina. The provincial sales tax does not apply to road fuel, but the 5% GST does, on the price that already includes the 15 cents. The federal excise is suspended since April 20, 2026. What does a year of driving a pickup cost in Regina? The budget calculator on this page answers with your own distance. It uses the median combined rating of 2026 full-size pickups from Natural Resources Canada and prices the litres at the Regina estimate for tomorrow. Choosing a smaller class or entering your own rating from the EnerGuide label changes the result immediately. Is gas cheaper in Regina or in Winnipeg? Both cities have their own monthly Statistics Canada series, and the page brings both forward with the same Edmonton rack price, so their estimates are comparable. Taxes differ: Saskatchewan charges 15 cents a litre and Manitoba 12.5 cents, both with 5% GST. The comparison calculator shows the current gap for a fill-up and for a year.

saskatoon/en.text: Saskatoon averaged 175.5¢/L for regular in September 2026, 1.5¢/L above Regina; the estimate for October 22, 2026 is 178.0¢/L. Saskatoon and Regina pay the same Saskatchewan taxes, yet Statistics Canada publishes a separate monthly average for each, and the two do not always agree. In September 2026, regular gasoline averaged 175.5¢/L in Saskatoon, 1.5¢/L above Regina, while diesel was 236.7¢/L, 4.3¢/L below Regina. Because a monthly figure is several weeks old by the time it appears, this page moves it to October 22, 2026 using the change in the Edmonton rack price with GST and any dated tax change, which gives 178.0¢/L for regular. Run over 25 earlier months, the method was off by 3.2¢/L on average, while assuming no change from one month to the next was off by 6.6¢/L. In a Saskatoon litre, the 15-cent provincial fuel tax and the 5% GST make up 13.2% of the estimate; Saskatchewan does not charge its sales tax on road fuel, and the federal excise is suspended since April 20, 2026. Two cities, one tax system, two averages Saskatchewan has two cities in the Statistics Canada table of retail fuel prices, and because they share every tax, comparing them shows how much retail markets can differ inside one province. In the 13 months shown on this site, Saskatoon's regular average was above Regina's 2 times. The table gives this city's latest month, its source and its estimate for October 22, 2026. Natural Resources Canada also compiles weekly city prices, but they cannot be reproduced here; its weekly table is the place to read them. The estimate uses the same Edmonton rack price as Regina's, so the two estimates keep the gap of their last monthly averages. The tomorrow page lists that estimate for every city. Saskatoon or Regina, per tank For drivers who travel between the two cities on Highway 11, the useful question is what the gap is worth. The calculator puts it in dollars per tank and per year. Diesel can tell a different story from gasoline: in September 2026, Saskatoon diesel was 4.3¢/L below Regina, against 1.5¢/L above Regina for regular. The two fuels come from different refinery markets, so the city that is cheaper for one is not always cheaper for the other. The diesel page has the national picture. The tax in a Saskatoon litre Saskatoon pays Saskatchewan's fuel tax of 15 cents a litre and GST at 5%, 8.5¢/L at the estimated price. No municipal or transit levy applies, and the provincial sales tax is not charged on road fuel. Between its neighbours, Saskatoon sits in the middle on tax: Alberta collects no provincial fuel tax under its relief program for now, and Manitoba charges 12.5 cents. With GST, the Saskatchewan rate is worth 15.75¢/L at the pump, which is part of why prices in Saskatoon and Edmonton differ even though both estimates follow the same wholesale price. The next dated change is federal: the excise tax, suspended since April 20, 2026, returns at half rate on February 1, 2027 and in full on April 1, 2027 under Finance Canada's draft legislation. Thirteen months of Saskatoon prices From September 2025 to September 2026, the Saskatoon regular average went from 138.1¢/L to 175.5¢/L, a change of +37.4¢. The series is under the Open Government Licence and appears below with diesel. Your next fill-up A 55-litre fill-up at the estimate for October 22, 2026 costs $97.90. Enter the price on the sign at your station to get your own figure. For the market to the west, the Edmonton page explains the wholesale price that drives these estimates; to the east, see Winnipeg . Is gas more expensive in Saskatoon than in Regina? It depends on the month. The two cities pay identical taxes, so any gap between their Statistics Canada averages comes from the product and retail margins. This page counts, month by month over the period it shows, how often Saskatoon was the higher of the two, and compares the two estimates for tomorrow with the same method. How much does a fill-up cost in Saskatoon today? At the estimate for tomorrow, the page gives the cost of a 55-litre fill-up, and the calculator lets you enter the price on the station sign and the size of your tank. Each cent per litre is worth 55 cents on such a tank, so a station a few cents below the average saves a dollar or two per fill-up, not more. How have Saskatoon gas prices changed over the past year? The page shows the last thirteen monthly averages published by Statistics Canada for Saskatoon, newest first, and the change between the first and the last of them. Those months include one dated tax change: the suspension of the 10-cent federal excise tax on April 20, 2026. The rest of the movement follows the wholesale market.

winnipeg/en.text: Regular gasoline in Winnipeg averaged 171.5¢/L in September 2026 and is estimated at 174.0¢/L for October 22, 2026. Winnipeg's official open gas price is a monthly one: Statistics Canada's average for September 2026 is 171.5¢/L a litre for regular, 198.1¢/L for premium and 242.2¢/L for diesel, taxes included. Manitoba is the easternmost province whose estimate on this site follows the Edmonton wholesale price, published daily by the Government of Ontario; adding its change since September 2026, with GST, gives 174.0¢/L for October 22, 2026. Checked against 25 past months, that estimate missed the next Statistics Canada average by 2.4¢/L on average, against 6.9¢/L for repeating the previous month. Manitoba's fuel tax is back at 12.5 cents a litre since the 2024 tax holiday ended on January 1, 2025; the provincial sales tax does not apply to fuel, and with the 5% GST the taxes make up 11.9% of the estimated price. The federal excise tax has been suspended since April 20, 2026. A monthly benchmark for Winnipeg Statistics Canada publishes Winnipeg's average retail price for each fuel once a month. The newest month on October 21, 2026 is September 2026, and the table shows it with the source, the estimate for October 22, 2026 and the past error of the method. Premium sits 26.6¢/L above regular in the September 2026 averages. Because Manitoba's taxes per litre are the same for both grades of gasoline, that spread lies entirely in the product. Weekly prices compiled by Natural Resources Canada exist for Winnipeg but cannot be reproduced here. Where the estimate comes from Winnipeg is far from both refining centres used by the site, and the choice of reference matters. The page uses the Edmonton rack price, the same one that moves the estimates for the other Prairie cities. From its September 2026 average to its value of October 14, 2026, it moved by +2.4¢, or +2.5¢ at the pump with GST. No Manitoba tax changed between that month and tomorrow. The tomorrow page gives the same breakdown for every city, and the method page explains how the error column is calculated. Manitoba's fuel tax after the holiday Manitoba stopped collecting its fuel tax for the whole of 2024, then brought it back on January 1, 2025 at 12.5 cents a litre for gasoline and diesel. That is the rate in force, with no city surcharge in Winnipeg. The provincial sales tax does not apply to road fuel; GST at 5% does, on the price that already includes the provincial cents, which is 8.3¢/L at the estimate. To see the tax in a litre at the price on the sign of your own station, enter it below. The tax page sets Manitoba against the other provinces and follows the return of the federal excise, planned at half rate on February 1, 2027 and in full on April 1, 2027. Winnipeg against Toronto The comparison crosses the line between the two markets the site follows: the western one, measured monthly and carried forward with the Edmonton rack price, and the central one, surveyed every week by Ontario. Keep the dates in view when reading the gap, and remember that Ontario's lower per-litre tax is partly offset by its higher sales tax. The past year in Winnipeg Over the 13 months below, Winnipeg regular averaged 147.8¢/L. The Statistics Canada series is published under the Open Government Licence, and neighbouring Regina and Saskatoon have their own pages. Is the Manitoba gas tax holiday still in effect in Winnipeg? No. Manitoba suspended its fuel tax for 2024 and the holiday ended on January 1, 2025, when the rate went back to 12.5 cents a litre. What is suspended in 2026 is the federal excise tax, since April 20, 2026, which applies across Canada. The tax table on this page shows both lines as they stand for tomorrow. Why does the Winnipeg estimate follow Edmonton and not Toronto? The page needs a daily wholesale price close to the market that supplies the city, and the open rack prices published by Ontario cover Toronto, Thunder Bay and Edmonton. The site treats Manitoba as part of the western market and uses the Edmonton price for it, as for Saskatchewan, Alberta and B.C. The measured error over past months is shown next to the estimate. How does a Winnipeg litre compare with one in Toronto? The two cities use different official sources: a monthly Statistics Canada average for Winnipeg, a weekly Ontario survey for Toronto. The comparison on this page uses the estimate for Winnipeg and the latest survey for Toronto, with their dates. On tax, Manitoba charges 12.5 cents and 5% GST, Ontario 9 cents and 13% HST.

halifax/en.text: The maximum price for regular gasoline in Halifax is 193.1¢/L, in force since October 16, 2026; the next scheduled reset is on October 23, 2026. Gasoline and diesel prices in Halifax are capped. The Nova Scotia Energy Board sets a maximum pump price for each zone of the province, and Halifax is in Zone 1; the figure on this page is that maximum, taxes included, not an average of what stations charge, and a station may sell for less. The maximum in force since October 16, 2026 is 193.1¢/L for self-serve regular and 273.2¢/L for diesel. The Board sets new prices every Friday at 12:01 a.m. and sometimes mid-week, so no change is scheduled for October 22, 2026 and the current cap is also the estimate for that day. Premium is not on the list used here: its figure is the Statistics Canada monthly average, 210.2¢/L for September 2026, brought forward to 207.0¢/L with the wholesale price. The method, replayed on 25 months of that series, erred by 2.4¢/L on average. Taxes are 20.3% of the regular price: 15.5 cents of Nova Scotia fuel tax and 14% HST, the federal excise being suspended since April 20, 2026. A price ceiling, not an average Nova Scotia regulates gasoline and diesel prices. The Nova Scotia Energy Board publishes a maximum retail price for each zone of the province, and the Halifax area is Zone 1. That changes how to read the number: it is the highest price a station may post for self-serve fuel, taxes included, and the price you see on the sign can be lower but not higher. The table below states the source and date of each figure. Statistics Canada's monthly average for regular in Halifax, a measure of prices actually charged, was 193.2¢/L for September 2026. Set against the cap now in force, that is +0.1¢, though the two cover different periods: a month of prices paid on one side, a ceiling for the current week on the other. The Friday reset The Board resets prices every Friday at 12:01 a.m., and sometimes mid-week as well when the market moves enough. The current cap took effect on October 16, 2026; the next scheduled reset falls on October 23, 2026. Since no reset is scheduled for October 22, 2026, the estimate for that day is simply the cap in force. Between resets, stations can change their price as they like, as long as it stays at or below the maximum. For a Halifax driver the practical consequence is timing. Because the cap is reset from wholesale prices, a week of falling wholesale prices points to a lower cap on Friday and a week of rising ones to a higher cap; filling only what you need before a reset that looks lower can save a little. The outlook page follows the wholesale trend. Premium in Halifax The cap the site reads for Zone 1 covers regular and diesel. For premium the page falls back on Statistics Canada's monthly average, 210.2¢/L for September 2026. The month is over, so the figure is carried to today with the change in the wholesale price and any dated tax change, which gives 207.0¢/L. It is an estimate, and labelled as one. Taxes in a Halifax litre Nova Scotia charges 15.5 cents a litre of motive fuel tax on gasoline and 15.4 cents on diesel, and HST has been 14% since April 1, 2025. The federal excise tax is suspended for now and due back in two steps in 2027. Halifax against Moncton New Brunswick also caps prices, with one maximum for the whole province. The current New Brunswick cap for regular is 191.8¢/L, so −1.3¢ relative to Halifax. Both are ceilings, so the comparison is between two maximums, not two averages. Moncton and St. John’s have their own pages. When do gas prices change in Halifax? The Nova Scotia Energy Board resets the maximum price every Friday at 12:01 a.m., and sometimes adjusts it mid-week as well. Stations may change their own price at any time as long as they stay at or below the maximum. The current Zone 1 cap has been in force since October 16, 2026. Can a Halifax gas station charge less than the maximum price? Yes. The regulated figure is a ceiling, not a fixed price. Stations in Halifax are free to sell below it, and nothing in the public data says how far below any one of them sits. That is why this page calls the number a maximum and never an average price paid at the pump. Why does Halifax premium gas use a different source? The page draws its Zone 1 maximums for regular and diesel from the Board, and does not read a premium maximum from that feed. For premium it uses Statistics Canada's monthly Halifax average instead, 210.2¢/L for September 2026, and brings it forward to today with the wholesale price and the dated taxes. It is an estimate, labelled as one.

moncton/en.text: In Moncton the maximum price for self-serve regular is 191.8¢/L this week, set on October 16, 2026 for all of New Brunswick. Moncton has no gas price average of its own because New Brunswick regulates the price instead. Each Friday at 12:01 a.m. the New Brunswick Energy and Utilities Board sets one maximum for the whole province, so Moncton, Saint John and Fredericton share the same ceiling. The maximum in force since October 16, 2026 is 191.8¢/L for self-serve regular, 230.3¢/L for premium and 273.4¢/L for diesel, taxes included. A retailer may add a delivery charge of up to 4.75 cents, so the highest legal posted price for regular is 196.6¢/L, while a station may also sell below the cap. No reset falls on October 22, 2026, so tomorrow's estimate is the current cap; the next scheduled one is October 23, 2026. Tested on 25 months of Statistics Canada's Saint John series, the estimation method missed by 2.3¢/L on average. Of the regular cap, 18.7% is tax: 10.87 cents of provincial tax and 15% HST, the federal excise being suspended since April 20, 2026. One ceiling for the whole province New Brunswick is one of the provinces that regulates pump prices, and it does so with a single maximum for all of its territory. The New Brunswick Energy and Utilities Board publishes it every Friday. Moncton has no other official price: the figures below are those caps, taxes included, dated from the Friday they took effect. Because the number is a ceiling, it describes the most a station may charge, not what most stations charge. Statistics Canada's monthly average for Saint John, the closest measure of prices actually paid, was 192.5¢/L for September 2026, +0.7¢ from the cap now in force; the two cover different periods. The delivery charge on top of the cap New Brunswick's rules let a retailer add a delivery charge of up to 4.75 cents a litre to the regulated maximum. It does not have to be charged, and the Board's figure does not include it. That gives a range for this week in Moncton: The fill-up calculator below takes the price on the sign, which already includes any delivery charge the station applies. The weekly cycle The Board sets the new maximums on Friday at 12:01 a.m. The current ones date from October 16, 2026, and the next scheduled change is on October 23, 2026. For October 22, 2026 there is no reset, so the estimate repeats the cap. Because each new ceiling follows the wholesale market of the previous days, the tomorrow page and the wholesale trend give a hint of the direction of the next one, but only the Board's publication fixes it. The cap also moves with tax changes dated in advance. The return of the federal excise, at half rate on February 1, 2027 and in full on April 1, 2027 under Finance Canada's draft legislation, would raise the ceiling itself, since the published maximum includes every tax, with HST at 15% charged on top of the excise. What a Moncton litre pays in tax New Brunswick's gasoline tax is 10.87 cents a litre and its motive fuel tax on diesel 15.45 cents. HST at 15% applies to the full price. At the current caps, taxes are 18.7% of a litre of regular and 18.7% of a litre of diesel. Moncton against Halifax Nova Scotia regulates too, by zone. The Halifax cap for regular is 193.1¢/L, which is +1.3¢ relative to New Brunswick's. The two provinces tax fuel differently, and the comparison is between ceilings, not averages. See the Halifax page , the St. John’s page and the provincial tax comparison . Is the gas price in Moncton the same as in Saint John and Fredericton? The maximum is the same. The New Brunswick Energy and Utilities Board sets one ceiling for the whole province every Friday, so Moncton, Saint John and Fredericton share it. Posted prices can still differ: a station may sell below the cap, and may add a delivery charge of up to 4.75 cents a litre on top of it. What is the delivery charge on gas in Moncton? New Brunswick's rules allow a retailer to add up to 4.75 cents a litre to the regulated maximum to cover delivery. With it, the most a Moncton station can legally post for regular this week is 196.6¢/L. On a 55-litre fill-up, the full charge would add $2.61. What day do gas prices change in Moncton? Friday. The Board publishes the new maximums for the week and they take effect at 12:01 a.m. that day. The current cap has applied since October 16, 2026, and the next scheduled change is on October 23, 2026. Between those dates, stations may lower their posted price but not raise it above the cap.

st-johns/en.text: The maximum price for self-serve regular in St. John's is 205.8¢/L, set by the Public Utilities Board for Zone 1 on October 21, 2026. St. John's gas prices are capped by the Board of Commissioners of Public Utilities of Newfoundland and Labrador, which sets a maximum for each zone; St. John's is in Zone 1, the Avalon Peninsula. The figure here is that ceiling, taxes included, and stations may sell below it. The cap dated October 21, 2026 is 205.8¢/L for self-serve regular and 278.6¢/L for diesel. The Board normally resets prices every Friday, but since October 2026 it has been setting them every day because of market volatility, so a new maximum is expected for October 22, 2026 and the page repeats the current one until it is published. Premium is taken from Statistics Canada's monthly average for St. John's, 219.5¢/L for September 2026, brought to 216.2¢/L with the wholesale change; over 25 months the method erred by 2.0¢/L on average. Tax is 16.7% of a litre of regular: 7.5 cents of provincial gasoline tax and 15% HST, the federal excise being suspended since April 20, 2026. The Zone 1 cap Newfoundland and Labrador divides the province into pricing zones, and the Board of Commissioners of Public Utilities sets a maximum retail price in each. St. John's belongs to Zone 1, on the Avalon Peninsula. The price on a sign in the city can be lower than this cap, never higher, and the cap already includes all taxes. For a measure of what was actually paid, Statistics Canada's monthly average for regular in St. John's was 213.7¢/L for September 2026. Set against the cap dated October 21, 2026, that is +7.9¢, but the two describe different periods, a past month and the current day. A daily reset, for now The Board's usual rhythm is weekly, with new maximums each Friday. Since October 2026 it has been resetting them every day because of market volatility, which means the St. John's cap can change overnight. A new maximum is therefore expected for October 22, 2026. Until it is published, the page keeps the cap in force rather than guessing the next one. When the Board returns to its weekly schedule, the page will follow it. Diesel on the Avalon Diesel is capped at 278.6¢/L, 72.8¢/L above regular. Part of the gap is tax: the province charges 9.5 cents a litre on diesel against 7.5 on gasoline, rates made permanent by a statute assented on March 30, 2026, and HST at 15% then applies to a higher base. Taxes are 16.5% of the diesel cap. The federal excise on diesel, 4 cents a litre before its suspension, is lower than on gasoline. When it returns in full on April 1, 2027 under Finance Canada's draft legislation, it adds 4.60¢/L with HST on diesel and 11.50¢/L on gasoline. The diesel page covers the fuel nationally. Premium, from a different source The Zone 1 cap the site reads covers regular and diesel only, so premium comes from Statistics Canada's monthly average for St. John's: 219.5¢/L for September 2026, carried to 216.2¢/L with the wholesale change since then. It is an estimate and is labelled so. Filling up at the cap Because the cap is the highest price allowed, it gives an upper bound on what a fill-up can cost in St. John's this week. A 55-litre tank of regular costs at most $113.19, a 90-litre pickup tank of diesel at most $250.74. If the sign shows less, enter it below to see the actual bill. St. John's in the Atlantic Nova Scotia and New Brunswick regulate too. Their current caps for regular are 193.1¢/L in Halifax and 191.8¢/L across New Brunswick . The provincial rates are compared on the tax page . Why do gas prices in St. John’s change every day right now? The Public Utilities Board normally sets new maximum prices once a week, on Friday. Since October 2026 it has been setting them every day, citing volatility in the market. As long as that lasts, the cap for St. John’s and the rest of the Avalon can change overnight, and the figure on this page is dated so you can see which day it belongs to. What is the maximum diesel price in St. John’s today? The Zone 1 cap for diesel, dated October 21, 2026, is 278.6¢/L, taxes included. Newfoundland and Labrador taxes diesel at 9.5 cents a litre before HST, more than gasoline. A 90-litre pickup tank filled at the full cap costs $250.74. Is gas more expensive in St. John’s than in Halifax or Moncton? On the current caps, St. John's regular at 205.8¢/L is +12.7¢ against Halifax and +14.0¢ against New Brunswick. All three are regulated maximums set on different schedules, so the comparison holds for the dates shown and can shift with the next reset in any of the three provinces.
